national.title: How to Get a Learner's Licence in India (2026)
national.summary: Complete document checklist, ₹200 official statutory fee breakdown, and step-by-step application instructions for Learner Licence across all Indian states.

steps.title: Submit Form 2 on the Sarathi Parivahan Portal
steps.description: Go to parivahan.gov.in, choose your State, and select 'Apply for Learner Licence'. Fill out your applicant details, address, and select vehicle class (MCWG for geared motorcycle, LMV for car).
steps.calloutText: If your mobile number is linked to Aadhaar, choose 'Applicant with Aadhaar' for paperless online verification without an in-person RTO visit for document submission.

steps.title: Upload Required Documents & Photo
steps.description: Upload scanned copies of Proof of Age, Proof of Address, and Form 1 (Self-declaration of physical fitness). If not using Aadhaar e-KYC, upload your signature and passport-size photograph.

steps.title: Pay Government Fee (₹200)
steps.description: Pay the statutory fee of ₹150 for application processing plus ₹50 for computerized test fee via net banking, debit card, or UPI. Download and print payment receipt Form 2.
steps.calloutText: Print the e-receipt immediately. The transaction reference number is required if payment status enters 'Pending'.

steps.title: Take the Computerized Learner Test (LL Test)
steps.description: Take the 15-question test on traffic signs and road safety. You have 30 seconds per question; score at least 11/15 (60%) to pass. On passing, your digital learner licence (Form 3) is generated instantly.
steps.where: Online from home (for Aadhaar e-KYC applicants) or at designated RTO Sub-Center

steps.title: Download & Print Your Digital Learner Licence (Form 3)
steps.description: Immediately upon scoring 11 or higher on the online test, your digital Learner Licence in Form 3 is generated with a verifiable QR code. Download the PDF and keep a physical printout while practicing driving with an instructor.
steps.calloutText: Traffic police and licensing authorities verify learner licences by scanning the QR code directly using their handheld mParivahan terminals.

faqItems.question: How long is a Learner's Licence valid in India?
faqItems.answer: A Learner's Licence is valid for exactly 6 months (180 days) from the date of issue across all states and Union Territories.

faqItems.question: Can I drive alone on public roads with a Learner's Licence?
faqItems.answer: No. You must be accompanied by someone who holds a valid permanent driving licence for that vehicle. Also, your vehicle must display red 'L' plates on front and back.

faqItems.question: What is the passing mark for the online Learner Licence test in India?
faqItems.answer: The computerized learner test consists of 15 multiple-choice questions covering Indian road signs, traffic signals, and fundamental driving regulations. You must answer at least 11 questions correctly (60% score) within the allotted 30 seconds per question to pass.

faqItems.question: When can I apply for a permanent driving licence after getting my learner licence?
faqItems.answer: You can apply for a permanent driving licence after 30 days from your Learner Licence issue date. You must apply within 180 days (6 months) before the learner licence expires.

rejectionReasons.title: Name or Date of Birth Mismatch on Aadhaar
rejectionReasons.description: If the name on your 10th marksheet or birth certificate does not match the name returned by Aadhaar e-KYC, the application is halted.
rejectionReasons.solution: Update your Aadhaar details first at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra, or apply via non-Aadhaar mode with physical document scrutiny at the RTO.

national.title: How to Apply for a Permanent Driving Licence in India (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step procedure to convert your Learner's Licence into a Permanent Driving Licence. Complete document checklist, official government fees (₹700), and driving test rules.

steps.title: Complete 30-Day Mandatory Waiting Period
steps.description: Wait at least 30 days after your Learner's Licence (LLR) was issued. Make sure your LLR has not expired (valid for 180 days).

steps.title: Submit Form 2 Application on Sarathi Parivahan
steps.description: Visit sarathi.parivahan.gov.in, select your State, and click 'Apply for Driving Licence'. Enter your Learner's Licence number and date of birth to load your details automatically.

steps.title: Select Vehicle Classes & Driving School Certificate
steps.description: Choose the vehicle classes endorsed on your learner permit (e.g. Motorcycle with Gear - MCWG, Light Motor Vehicle - LMV). If you were trained at an accredited driver training institute (ADTC), upload your Form 5B certificate.
steps.calloutText: Under Section 12 of the Motor Vehicles Act, candidates with a Form 5B certificate from an Accredited Driving School skip the practical RTO driving test.

steps.title: Pay Statutory Government Fees Online
steps.description: Pay ₹200 for DL issue, ₹200 for smart card printing, and ₹300 per vehicle class test fee. Total is ₹700 for single class or ₹1,000 for dual class.

steps.title: Book Practical Driving Test Appointment Slot
steps.description: Select your designated RTO or Automated Driving Test Track (ADTT) and pick an available date and time slot. Download and print the Appointment Slip.

steps.title: Appear for the Practical Driving Test at RTO Track
steps.description: Arrive at the RTO test track 30 minutes before your slot with a vehicle corresponding to your application category. For two-wheelers, demonstrate figure-of-eight (8) balancing and sudden stopping. For four-wheelers, pass the H-track reverse parking, parallel parking, and gradient hill restart without rolling backwards.
steps.where: RTO Driving Test Track / ADTT Center
steps.calloutText: The vehicle you bring for the test must have valid physical registration certificate (RC), active insurance policy, and valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate.

steps.title: Test Results and Biometric Data Verification
steps.description: If you pass the test, the testing officer signs your inspection sheet or the automated track sensors submit an instant electronic pass report. Your digital photo and signature are verified.

steps.title: Receive Driving Licence via Speed Post & DigiLocker
steps.description: Your permanent driving licence number is generated within 24-48 hours and available on DigiLocker and mParivahan. The physical chip-based Smart Card licence is printed and dispatched to your residential address via India Post Speed Post.
steps.calloutText: Once your DL number is generated, your digital driving licence in DigiLocker or mParivahan is legally valid across India under CMVR Rule 139.

faqItems.question: When can I apply for a permanent driving licence after getting a learner's licence?
faqItems.answer: You can apply exactly 30 days after the date your learner licence was issued. You have up to 180 days (6 months) from the LL issuance date to pass the driving test and obtain your permanent licence.

faqItems.question: What happens if I fail the practical driving test?
faqItems.answer: If you fail the test, you can re-appear for a re-test after a mandatory 7-day practice period. You will need to log into Sarathi Parivahan, pay a re-test fee of ₹300, and book a new appointment slot.

faqItems.question: Can I take the driving test in an automatic transmission car?
faqItems.answer: Yes! You can bring either a manual or an automatic transmission vehicle for your test. However, you must arrange the vehicle yourself; RTOs do not provide test vehicles.

faqItems.question: What is the validity period of a permanent driving licence in India?
faqItems.answer: For private vehicles, a driving licence is valid for 20 years or until age 40, whichever is earlier. For ages 40 to 50, it is valid for 10 years. For ages 50 to 55, it is valid until age 60. Above age 55, it is renewed every 5 years.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying Before 30-Day Mandatory Waiting Period
rejectionReasons.description: Attempting to book a permanent DL test slot when less than 30 days have elapsed since the learner licence was approved.
rejectionReasons.solution: Wait until day 31 from the date printed on your Learner Licence Form 3 before scheduling.

rejectionReasons.title: Expired Test Vehicle Documentation
rejectionReasons.description: Bringing a vehicle to the test track with expired third-party insurance or expired PUC certificate leads to immediate test cancellation.
rejectionReasons.solution: Check mParivahan on your phone to verify the vehicle's fitness, insurance, and PUC are active before visiting the track.

rejectionReasons.title: Failure on Automated Sensor Tracks (Touching Yellow Lines)
rejectionReasons.description: Automated sensor tracks register a fail if vehicle tyres cross boundary lines or exceed allowed forward-reverse maneuvers.
rejectionReasons.solution: Practice parallel parking and reverse H-parking beforehand without crossing side curbs.

national.title: How to Apply for a Fresh Indian Passport: Documents, Fees, and Steps (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step guide to applying for a first-time Indian passport online on the Passport Seva portal. Verified fees (₹1,500 normal, ₹3,500 tatkaal) and complete document checklist.

steps.title: Register on the Official Passport Seva Portal
steps.description: Visit passportindia.gov.in and register a new user account. Choose your Passport Office based on your present residential address.
steps.calloutText: Only apply on passportindia.gov.in. Never use private commercial websites that mimic the portal and charge unauthorized fees.

steps.title: Fill the Online Application for Fresh Passport
steps.description: Select 'Apply for Fresh Passport'. Choose between Normal or Tatkaal scheme and pick booklet size of 36 or 60 pages.

steps.title: Enter Personal, Family, and Address Details
steps.description: Fill your full name, date of birth, and parents' names accurately. Enter your current residential address with correct pin code.
steps.calloutText: Ensure spellings match your 10th marksheet or birth certificate exactly. Single letter mismatches cause delays at verification counters.

steps.title: Declare Emigration Check Status (Non-ECR)
steps.description: Choose Non-ECR if you have passed 10th standard or hold a higher degree. This removes emigration clearance checks for overseas travel.
steps.calloutText: Attach your 10th standard passing certificate to qualify for Non-ECR status automatically.

steps.title: Pay the Statutory Government Fee Online
steps.description: Pay ₹1,500 for normal 36 pages or ₹3,500 for Tatkaal scheme. Payment is processed securely via SBI ePay with Net Banking, UPI, or cards.

steps.title: Schedule Appointment at Nearest PSK or POPSK
steps.description: Select your preferred Passport Seva Kendra or Post Office Passport Seva Kendra. Pick an available date and time slot, then download the receipt.
steps.calloutText: The SMS confirmation on your mobile phone is officially accepted at the PSK entry gate.

steps.title: Attend PSK Appointment for Biometrics and Verification
steps.description: Arrive 15 minutes before your batch time with all original documents. Complete photograph at Counter A, verification at Counter B, and approval at Counter C.

steps.title: Complete Local Police Verification and Receive Passport
steps.description: The local police station will verify your physical address and identity. After police clearance, India Post delivers your passport via Speed Post.
steps.calloutText: Police verification requires applicant presence at home with original documents and two neighbourhood references.

faqItems.question: Who needs to apply for a Fresh Passport in India?
faqItems.answer: Any Indian citizen who has never held an Indian passport before must apply under the Fresh Passport category.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between Normal and Tatkaal passport schemes?
faqItems.answer: Normal processing takes 10 to 20 working days. Tatkaal processing issues the passport within 1 to 3 days for an extra fee.

faqItems.question: What does Non-ECR status mean on an Indian passport?
faqItems.answer: Non-ECR means Emigration Check Not Required. Citizens who passed 10th standard or hold higher degrees do not need clearance for employment abroad.

faqItems.question: Can I apply for a fresh passport without a municipal birth certificate?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Applicants born on or after 26 January 1989 can use Aadhaar, PAN card, or School Leaving Certificate as proof of birth date.

faqItems.question: Is an Aadhaar card compulsory to get a fresh passport?
faqItems.answer: Aadhaar is not strictly compulsory, but it is highly recommended. It serves as both identity and address proof and speeds up processing.

faqItems.question: How long does police verification take for a fresh passport?
faqItems.answer: Police verification typically takes 7 to 14 days depending on your local police station and district intelligence branch.

faqItems.question: Do adult applicants need to bring printed photographs to the PSK?
faqItems.answer: No. Adult photographs and fingerprints are captured live at Counter A inside the PSK. Only minors below 4 years need physical photos.

faqItems.question: How can I track my fresh passport status after the appointment?
faqItems.answer: Log in to passportindia.gov.in and click 'Track Application Status'. Enter your 15-digit File Number and date of birth to check progress.

rejectionReasons.title: Name or Date of Birth Mismatch on IDs
rejectionReasons.description: If your name or date of birth differs between Aadhaar and your birth certificate, the counter officer will halt processing.
rejectionReasons.solution: Update your Aadhaar details first at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra to match your educational certificate or legal birth record.

rejectionReasons.title: Address Verification Failure During Police Visit
rejectionReasons.description: If the applicant does not reside at the address or neighbours fail to verify stay, the police file an adverse report.
rejectionReasons.solution: Ensure you have lived at the declared address for at least one year and keep neighbours informed about your verification.

rejectionReasons.title: Failing to Declare Previous Application or Passport
rejectionReasons.description: Suppressing information about an earlier passport application or file number leads to system match flags and penalties.
rejectionReasons.solution: Always mention previous file numbers or passport details honestly in the application form.

rejectionReasons.title: Incomplete Minor Consent (Missing Annexure D)
rejectionReasons.description: A minor passport requires signatures and passports of both parents unless supported by court custody order.
rejectionReasons.solution: Submit Annexure D signed by both parents, or submit Annexure C if one parent is unavailable.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying for Tatkaal Without 3 Prescribed Documents
rejectionReasons.description: Tatkaal scheme requires three specific photo ID documents. If one is missing, the application is converted to Normal scheme.
rejectionReasons.solution: Check the official document advisor and carry Aadhaar, PAN card, and Voter ID or bank passbook.

rejectionReasons.title: Unclear or Torn Original Documents
rejectionReasons.description: Laminated certificates with hidden seals or torn documents will be rejected by the Verifying Officer.
rejectionReasons.solution: Carry clean, legible original documents without peeling lamination or obscured stamps.

rejectionReasons.title: Unresolved Criminal Case or Pending Court Order
rejectionReasons.description: Section 6 of the Passports Act restricts passport issuance if criminal proceedings are pending before an Indian court.
rejectionReasons.solution: Obtain formal permission from the concerned court to travel abroad and attach the certified court order.

national.summary: Step-by-step procedure to re-issue an expired or expiring Indian passport online through the official Passport Seva portal. Verified fees (₹1,500 normal, ₹3,500 tatkaal) and document rules.

steps.title: Register or Log In to Official Passport Seva Portal
steps.description: Visit passportindia.gov.in and select your Passport Office based on your current city. Register a new account or log in with existing credentials.
steps.calloutText: Only apply on passportindia.gov.in. Never use unauthorized commercial websites that mimic the portal and charge illegitimate consulting fees.

steps.title: Select 'Apply for Fresh Passport / Re-issue of Passport'
steps.description: Click 'Apply for Fresh Passport / Re-issue of Passport'. Select 'Re-issue', choose your reason, and pick booklet size (36 or 60 pages) and scheme.

steps.title: Fill the Online Application Form Details
steps.description: Enter your applicant details, family details (father, mother, spouse), current residential address, emergency contact, and existing passport number, issue date, and expiry date. Provide details of two local references residing in your neighbourhood.
steps.calloutText: If you passed 10th standard or hold a degree, select Non-ECR. This avoids emigration check restrictions when travelling overseas.

steps.title: Pay Government Statutory Fee Online
steps.description: Click 'Pay and Schedule Appointment'. Pay ₹1,500 (36 pages) or ₹2,000 (60 pages) online via Net Banking, Card, or UPI. Payment is mandatory to book a slot.

steps.title: Schedule Appointment at Nearest PSK or POPSK
steps.description: Select your nearest Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) or Post Office Passport Seva Kendra (POPSK) and choose an available date and time slot. Print or download the Application Receipt showing your ARN and appointment batch time.
steps.calloutText: Carrying an SMS appointment confirmation on your mobile phone with ARN is officially accepted at the PSK entrance gate in lieu of a paper printout.

steps.title: Visit the PSK with Original Documents
steps.description: Arrive 15 minutes before your appointment time. You will visit Counter A for biometrics, Counter B for document verification, and Counter C for approval.

steps.title: Undergo Local Police Verification
steps.description: If current address has changed, local police station conducts in-person physical address verification. The police officer visits your residence to check original address proof and verify your two local references.

steps.title: Receive Renewed Passport via Speed Post
steps.description: Once police verification report (PVR) is cleared, your passport is printed at the India Security Press and dispatched via India Post Speed Post. You will receive an SMS with the Speed Post tracking consignment number.
steps.calloutText: Your old passport will be physically cancelled by the PSK officer (corners clipped) and handed back to you at Counter C. Any valid unexpired visas inside remain legally valid.

faqItems.question: How early before expiry can I apply for passport renewal in India?
faqItems.answer: You can apply up to 1 year before your passport expires. We recommend applying 6 to 9 months before expiry because many countries require 6 months validity.

faqItems.question: What happens to valid visas inside my old cancelled passport?
faqItems.answer: Your valid visas remain completely valid! The passport officer will only cancel the passport booklet itself by punching holes in the corners, leaving intact any pages containing active visas. When travelling abroad, simply carry both your new passport and the old cancelled passport containing the valid visa.

faqItems.question: Is police verification mandatory for every passport renewal?
faqItems.answer: Not always. If you apply within 3 years of expiry with no address change, police verification is usually waived or done post-issuance. If your address changed, pre-verification is required.

faqItems.question: Can I renew my passport under Tatkaal scheme?
faqItems.answer: Yes! Tatkaal renewal is available for urgent travel needs with an additional fee of ₹2,000. Tatkaal passports are dispatched within 1 to 3 working days from the date of application at the PSK. However, Tatkaal is not permitted if the passport has been expired for more than 3 years, lost, damaged, or if major name changes are requested.

faqItems.question: What if my passport has already expired for more than 3 years?
faqItems.answer: If your passport expired more than 3 years ago, renewal is still permitted but requires mandatory pre-issuance police verification. You will also be asked to provide an explanation letter stating the reason for late renewal.

faqItems.question: How do I add my spouse's name upon renewal?
faqItems.answer: In the online application form, select 'Add/Change Spouse Name' and enter your spouse's name. You must carry your Marriage Certificate or an unexpired passport of your spouse showing your name as spouse.

faqItems.question: Do I need to carry passport-size photos to the PSK?
faqItems.answer: For adults and children above 4 years of age, physical photos are NOT required. Your digital photograph and biometric fingerprints are captured live at Counter A inside the PSK. Only for infants and children under 4 years of age, parents must carry one recent passport-size color photograph with a plain white background.

faqItems.question: How can I track the delivery status of my new passport?
faqItems.answer: You can track your application online on passportindia.gov.in using your 15-digit File Number / ARN. Once dispatched, an India Post Speed Post tracking number (Consignment Number) will be sent via SMS and displayed on the status page.

rejectionReasons.title: Address Mismatch Between Document Proof and Application
rejectionReasons.description: Entering an address in the form that does not match your proof document will cause verification rejection. Always use an exact matching address document.
rejectionReasons.solution: Ensure the current address typed into the form matches character-by-character with the utility bill or Aadhaar card submitted.

rejectionReasons.title: Unclear or Missing Pages in Old Passport Photocopy
rejectionReasons.description: Failing to photocopy both the first two pages and the last two pages, or submitting illegible blurred copies.
rejectionReasons.solution: Make clear, legible photocopies of pages 1, 2, 35, and 36, and self-attest each sheet with your signature.

rejectionReasons.title: Failed Police Verification Due to Absence from Residence
rejectionReasons.description: When the local beat police officer visits your residence and neighbours report that you do not reside there or you cannot be contacted.
rejectionReasons.solution: Provide active mobile numbers and ensure your two neighbourhood references are aware and available to verify your physical residence.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying Under Tatkaal Without Meeting Eligibility Criteria
rejectionReasons.description: Tatkaal applications where the applicant has had major name changes, or whose previous passport was damaged or lost.
rejectionReasons.solution: Check the official Tatkaal eligibility checklist on Passport Seva before choosing the Tatkaal scheme; otherwise apply under Normal.

rejectionReasons.title: Undisclosed Criminal Proceedings or Pending Court Cases
rejectionReasons.description: Suppressing information regarding pending FIRs or criminal court summons violates Section 12 of the Passports Act 1967.
rejectionReasons.solution: Always disclose pending matters and obtain an explicit No Objection Certificate (NOC) or court order permitting passport re-issue.

rejectionReasons.title: Failure to Attend Rescheduled Appointments within 1 Year
rejectionReasons.description: Missing scheduled appointment dates without attending a PSK within the 1-year application fee validity window leads to fee forfeiture.
rejectionReasons.solution: Reschedule your appointment online if unable to attend. You are permitted up to 3 appointment reschedules within 12 months from payment date.

national.title: How to Get Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) for Abroad: Steps & Fees (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step guide to applying for a Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) online through Passport Seva. Verified statutory fee of ₹500, required documents, and police verification steps.

steps.title: Log In to the Official Passport Seva Portal
steps.description: Visit passportindia.gov.in and log in with your existing account. If you do not have an account, complete user registration.
steps.calloutText: Only apply on passportindia.gov.in. Commercial intermediary sites charge extra fees without official authorization.

steps.title: Select 'Apply for Police Clearance Certificate'
steps.description: Click 'Apply for Police Clearance Certificate'. Enter your valid Indian passport number, issue date, and passport expiry date.

steps.title: Fill Country and Visa Purpose Details
steps.description: Select the destination country and specify your visa category. Common categories include employment, immigration, long-term stay, or overseas student visa.
steps.calloutTitle: Tourist Visas Do Not Need PCC
steps.calloutText: PCC is strictly for long-term stay, study, or work visas. Regular short tourist visits do not require a PCC.

steps.title: Pay the Statutory Government Fee of ₹500
steps.description: Pay the mandatory ₹500 statutory fee online through SBI ePay. You can use UPI, debit cards, or net banking.

steps.title: Schedule Appointment at Nearest PSK or POPSK
steps.description: Choose an available date and time slot at your nearest Passport Seva Kendra or Post Office PSK. Download your appointment receipt.
steps.calloutText: The official SMS received on your registered mobile number is accepted for entry at the PSK security gate.

steps.title: Visit PSK for Physical Document Scrutiny
steps.description: Visit the PSK with your original passport and self-attested photocopies. The officer verifies your passport authenticity and takes digital biometric acknowledgement.

steps.title: Undergo Verification at Local Police Station
steps.description: Your local jurisdiction police station receives the electronic enquiry. An officer conducts physical address verification and background criminal records check.
steps.calloutText: Police verification officers typically request two local neighbourhood references to confirm your residential stay.

steps.title: Collect Issued Police Clearance Certificate
steps.description: Once clear police report uploads, your PCC certificate is issued. You will receive an SMS to collect the physical certificate or track Speed Post delivery.
steps.where: Passport Seva Kendra or Delivered via Speed Post

faqItems.question: What is a Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) from Passport Seva?
faqItems.answer: A PCC is an official document issued by the Ministry of External Affairs certifying that an Indian citizen has no adverse criminal record.

faqItems.question: Who needs to apply for a Police Clearance Certificate?
faqItems.answer: Indian citizens moving abroad for employment, long-term immigration, permanent residency, or higher education require a PCC.

faqItems.question: Can I obtain a PCC if my Indian passport has expired?
faqItems.answer: No. You must renew your expired passport first before applying for a Police Clearance Certificate.

faqItems.question: What is the official statutory fee for a PCC?
faqItems.answer: The statutory fee is ₹500 paid online through the official Passport Seva portal.

faqItems.question: How long is an Indian Police Clearance Certificate valid?
faqItems.answer: The certificate is generally valid for 6 months from the date of issue for most foreign embassy visa applications.

faqItems.question: Do tourists going abroad on vacation need a PCC?
faqItems.answer: No. Short tourist visa holders do not require a Police Clearance Certificate.

faqItems.question: Is there a Tatkaal urgent scheme for PCC issuance?
faqItems.answer: No. PCC applications must undergo mandatory local police verification, so no Tatkaal quota is available.

faqItems.question: Can I apply if my current address differs from my passport address?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Provide valid proof of your current address, such as an Aadhaar Card or utility bill, when filling out the form.

rejectionReasons.title: Pending Criminal Case or Active Court Warrant
rejectionReasons.description: If an active FIR, chargesheet, or court summon exists in your name, the local police will issue an adverse report.
rejectionReasons.solution: Obtain formal clearance from the concerned court before applying for foreign clearance.

rejectionReasons.title: Address Mismatch with Police Station Jurisdiction
rejectionReasons.description: Selecting a police station that does not have administrative jurisdiction over your actual residence results in file return.
rejectionReasons.solution: Verify your exact local police station limits with neighbours or local municipality before submitting Form 1.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying with an Expired Passport
rejectionReasons.description: PCC can only be issued against an active, valid Indian passport. Expired passports are rejected immediately.
rejectionReasons.solution: Apply for passport renewal first. Once your renewed passport is issued, apply for your PCC.

rejectionReasons.title: Applicant Not Found During Police Visit
rejectionReasons.description: If the verification officer visits and finds the house locked or neighbours deny knowing the applicant, the report is marked adverse.
rejectionReasons.solution: Keep your phone reachable, stay present in town, and inform family members to facilitate the verification.

rejectionReasons.title: Mutilated or Damaged Physical Passport
rejectionReasons.description: A passport with torn pages or damaged biographical laminate will be rejected during PSK counter verification.
rejectionReasons.solution: Apply for passport re-issue under 'Damaged Passport' category before seeking a police certificate.

rejectionReasons.title: Failing to Provide Supporting Visa Reason
rejectionReasons.description: The Ministry requires a valid purpose for issuing a PCC. Vague or undeclared travel plans will delay clearance.
rejectionReasons.solution: Attach your job contract, university admission letter, or visa checklist with your application.

glossary.defEn: A written statement sworn before an authorized notary or magistrate. It legally confirms that the facts stated by you are 100% true. Making a false affidavit is a criminal offense.
glossary.defHi: नोटरी या मजिस्ट्रेट के सामने शपथ लेकर दिया गया लिखित बयान। यह कानूनी रूप से पुष्टि करता है कि आपके द्वारा दी गई जानकारी सच है।
glossary.defGu: નોટરી અથવા મેજિસ્ટ્રેટ સમક્ષ સોગંદપૂર્વક કરાયેલું લેખિત નિવેદન, જે કાયદેસર રીતે સાબિત કરે છે કે તમારી માહિતી સંપૂર્ણપણે સાચી છે.
glossary.whoIssues: Drafted on non-judicial stamp paper and signed before an Executive Magistrate or Notary Public.
glossary.commonCost: ₹50 or ₹100 stamp paper + ₹50 notary attestation fee.
glossary.tips: Always check the required stamp paper denomination (e.g., ₹50 vs ₹100) before buying.

glossary.defEn: A government-appointed legal officer (advocate) authorized to verify your identity, witness your signature, and place an official seal and stamp on legal declarations.
glossary.defHi: सरकार द्वारा अधिकृत वकील जो आपकी पहचान की पुष्टि करता है, आपके हस्ताक्षर देखता है और दस्तावेजों पर आधिकारिक मुहर लगाता है।
glossary.defGu: સરકાર દ્વારા અધિકૃત વકીલ જે તમારી અસલ ઓળખ ચકાસીને તમારા દસ્તાવેજ પર સહી તથા સત્તાવાર સિક્કો મારે છે.
glossary.whoIssues: Advocates appointed as Notaries by the Central or State Law Department.
glossary.tips: Ensure the notary writes their registration number and expiry date next to their seal.

glossary.defEn: The official government publication where new statutes, statutory fee revisions, and legal name changes are published to make them legally recognized across India.
glossary.defHi: सरकार का आधिकारिक प्रकाशन जहां नए कानून, सरकारी फीस और नाम बदलने की सूचनाएं कानूनी रूप से प्रकाशित होती हैं।
glossary.defGu: સરકારનું સત્તાવાર પ્રકાશન જેમાં નવા કાયદા, સરકારી ફી અને નામ બદલવાની જાહેરાતો કાયદેસર રીતે જાહેર થાય છે.
glossary.whoIssues: Department of Publication, Government of India (Central Gazette) or State Government Printing Press.
glossary.tips: Download digital e-Gazette copies directly from egazette.gov.in free of cost.

glossary.defEn: Writing 'Self-Attested' on a photocopy, followed by your regular signature and the current date. It certifies that the photocopy is a true copy of your original document. No gazetted officer or seal is required.
glossary.defHi: फोटोकॉपी पर 'Self-Attested' लिखकर अपने खुद के हस्ताक्षर और तारीख डालना। इसके लिए किसी सरकारी अफसर की मुहर की जरूरत नहीं होती।
glossary.defGu: ઝેરોક્ષ કોપી પર 'Self-Attested' લખીને તમારી પોતાની સહી અને તારીખ કરવી. આ માટે કોઈ સરકારી અધિકારીની સહીની જરૂર નથી હોતી.
glossary.tips: Sign across the blank margin without obscuring vital document details or photo.

glossary.defEn: An official certificate issued by the state revenue department certifying that a person has been residing permanently in that particular state for a specified duration (usually 10 to 15 years).
glossary.defHi: राज्य के राजस्व विभाग द्वारा जारी प्रमाण पत्र जो यह साबित करता है कि आप उस राज्य के स्थायी निवासी हैं।
glossary.defGu: મહેસૂલ વિભાગ દ્વારા અપાતું પ્રમાણપત્ર જે સાબિત કરે છે કે તમે ઘણા વર્ષોથી રાજ્યમાં કાયમી રહેવાસી છો.
glossary.commonCost: ₹20 – ₹50 statutory fee on state citizen portal.
glossary.tips: Electricity bills, school leaving certificates, and parent's voter ID are commonly accepted proofs.

glossary.defEn: An official document issued by a government authority, employer, or financer stating that they have zero objection to a requested transaction or application.
glossary.defHi: संबंधित विभाग या बैंक द्वारा जारी दस्तावेज जिसमें लिखा होता है कि आपके आवेदन या ट्रांसफर से उन्हें कोई आपत्ति नहीं है।
glossary.defGu: સંબંધિત વિભાગ કે બેંક દ્વારા અપાતો દસ્તાવેજ જેમાં દર્શાવાય છે કે તમારી અરજી સામે તેમને કોઈ વાંધો નથી.
glossary.whoIssues: RTO (Form 28 for vehicle transfer), Police department, or financing bank.
glossary.tips: Ensure vehicle NOC from RTO is used within its validity period (usually 6 months).

glossary.defEn: An official expedited fast-track government scheme that delivers passports or public services in 1 to 3 business days for an additional gazetted surcharge.
glossary.defHi: आपातकालीन त्वरित सेवा जो अतिरिक्त सरकारी शुल्क लेकर 1 से 3 दिनों में पासपोर्ट या दस्तावेज तैयार करती है।
glossary.defGu: સરકારી કટોકટી સેવા જે વધારાની સરકારી ફી લઈને ૧ થી ૩ દિવસમાં પાસપોર્ટ કે દસ્તાવેજ આપવાની સુવિધા આપે છે.
glossary.whoIssues: Passport Seva Kendra (Ministry of External Affairs).
glossary.tips: Police verification for Tatkaal passports happens after dispatch (Post-police verification).

glossary.defEn: A standardized affidavit or declaration form attached to a government application to certify specific circumstances (such as citizenship declaration, spouse details, or lost document explanation).
glossary.defHi: आवेदन के साथ लगने वाला आधिकारिक हलफनामा या घोषणा पत्र प्रारूप (जैसे पासपोर्ट के लिए Annexure E)।
glossary.defGu: અરજી સાથે જોડવાનું સત્તાવાર સોગંદનામું કે બાંયધરી ફોર્મ (જેમ કે પાસપોર્ટ માટે Annexure E).
glossary.whoIssues: Official format downloaded from the government portal and filled by the applicant.
glossary.commonCost: Free download; printed on plain paper or stamp paper as specified.
glossary.tips: Most passport annexures now only require self-declaration on plain paper rather than expensive stamp paper.

glossary.defEn: An official computerized receipt or payment demand note used to deposit statutory fees or penalties directly into the government treasury.
glossary.defHi: सरकारी खजाने में फीस या जुर्माना जमा करने की आधिकारिक रसीદ।
glossary.defGu: સરકારી તિજોરીમાં ફી અથવા દંડ જમા કરાવવાની સત્તાવાર કોમ્પ્યુટરાઈઝ્ડ રસીદ.
glossary.whoIssues: State treasury department, traffic police, or Parivahan portal.
glossary.commonCost: Matches the exact statutory fee or penalty.
glossary.tips: Always preserve the 16-digit Challan Reference Number (CIN / GRN) for payment tracking.
